header: IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT, LAHORE
J U D G M E N T
body: Date of hearing: 20.11.2026 Petitioner by:
Ch. Naseer Ahmad, Advocate alongwith Mr. Shahrukh Shahbaz Warraich, Advocate.
State/respondent No.1 by:
Ms. Nuzhat Bashir, Deputy Prosecutor General alongwith Shabbir, S.I.
Complainant/respondent No.2 by:

Faiza Bibi (complainant of the case/ respondent No.2 in the petition, identified by aforementioned police official) and Naveed Ali (injured of the case, also identified by aforementioned police official), in person.

FAROOQ HAIDER, J. :- Muhammad Ahsan alias Raju (petitioner) alongwith his co-accused namely Saqlain Abbas was tried in case arising out of F.I.R. No.353/2023 dated: 24.02.2023 registered under Sections: 324, 34 PPC {subsequently, offence under Section: 337-F(iii) PPC was added during the investigation} at Police Station: Tibbi City, District: Lahore and learned Judicial Magistrate Section: 30, Lahore (trial court) vide judgment dated: 22.04.2025 while acquitting the petitioner under Section: 34 PPC as well as acquitting aforementioned co-accused from the charges, convicted and sentenced the petitioner under Sections: 337-F(iii), 324 PPC; in this regard, relevant portion from the impugned judgment is hereby reproduced as under: - “16. Final decision. In light of the above discussion and findings on all the points of determination formulated above, the final conclusions are as follows: - Criminal Revision No.8944 of 2026 2 A. prosecution has failed to prove its allegations against the accused person Saqlain Abbas s/o Ghulam Abbas, beyond shadow of reasonable doubt. Thus, accused Saqlain Abbas s/o YGhulam Abbas is acquitted from the charges under sections 337-F(iii) and 324 of Pakistan Penal Code 1860 read with section 34 of Pakistan Penal Code 1860, leveled in case FIR no.353/2023 registered at P.S. Tibbi city, Lahore. Accused was on bail, surety stands discharged from the responsibility to produce the accused.

B. prosecution has failed to prove its allegation against the accused Ahsan alias Raju of committing this occurrence in furtherance of common intention, thus he is acquitted from the charge of sharing common intention under section 34 of Pakistan Penal Code, 1860. However, prosecution has successfully proved its allegation against the said accused regarding inflicting injury at the left thigh of injured Navid Ali with firearm weapon. Thus, he is convicted for offence punishable under section 337F(iii), PPC and for offence punishable under section 324, PPC. As far as quantum of sentence is concerned, he is sentenced to the following effect: i. to pay Duman of Rs.100,000/- to the injured Navid Ali s/o Aziz Ali and also to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a term of three years as Tazir for causing Jurh Ghayr-Jaifah Mutalahimah to the said injured which is punishable under section 337-F(iii) of Pakistan Penal code, 1860.
ii. to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a term of Seven Years for attempting to commit Qatl-i-Amd punishable under section 324 of Pakistan Penal code, 1860.

iii. to pay Rs.50,000/- as compensation to the injured Navid Ali under section 544-A of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. This amount shall be recoverable from the convict as arrears of land revenue and in case of his default to pay the compensation amount to the injured, he shall further undergo three months' simple imprisonment, in addition to any other sentence of imprisonment.
iv. Sentences of imprisonment shall run concurrently, except in case of default of payment of compensation amount.
v. benefit of section 382-B of Code of Criminal Procedure 1898 is also extended in favor of convict Ahsan alias Raju.”

Against aforementioned convictions and sentences, petitioner filed Criminal Appeal, which was dismissed vide impugned judgment dated: 17.01.2026 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (appellate Court) and resultantly convictions recorded and sentences awarded to the petitioner qua offences under Sections: 324, 337-F(iii) PPC were maintained. Feeling aggrieved, petitioner has filed instant criminal revision petition before this Court. Criminal Revision No.8944 of 2026 3 2. Briefly, the prosecution case as per Fard Bayan (Ex.PA) got recorded by Faiza Bibi (complainant/PW-1) to Iftikhar Ahmad, A.S.I., on the basis of which above mentioned F.I.R. (Ex.PB) was registered, is that Raju (present petitioner) while armed with pistol and accused Saqlain armed with pistol uttered abuses to Naveed Ali (husband of complainant lady); Raju raised lalkara and made straight firing at husband of complainant lady; one fire hit at thigh of right leg of Naveed and one fire hit at thigh of left leg whereas Saqlain fired shot with pistol which hit at left shin of Naveed, who after becoming injured, fell on the ground; Raju also gave Butt blows at face and head of Naveed, which caused injuries to Naveed. For ready reference, relevant portion of the crime report (F.I.R./Ex.PB) is reproduced as under: - After completion of investigation, petitioner and his aforementioned coaccused were challaned to the Court, they were formally charge sheeted, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Prosecution got examined ten witnesses, out of whom, ocular account was furnished by Faiza Bibi (complainant/PW-1), Muhammad Naveed (injured/PW-2) and Muhammad Naeem (eyewitness/PW-3), medical evidence was furnished by Dr. Haider Ali (PW-10) whereas Abid Hussain, S.I. (PW-5) and Muhammad Razzaq, S.I. (PW-6) deposed about investigation of the case. Thereafter statements of the petitioner and his co-accused were recorded under Section: 342 Cr.P.C. in Criminal Revision No.8944 of 2026 4 which they refuted the allegations levelled against them; they did not opt to appear as their own witnesses under Section: 340(2) Cr.P.C. however, petitioner produced some documents i.e. Ex.DA, Ex.DB as well as Mark-A and Mark-B in his defence.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that both the impugned judgments (mentioned above) are against the law as well as facts of the case; adds that prosecution remained unable to prove its case beyond shadow of reasonable doubt; finally prays for setting-aside the impugned judgments and acquittal of the petitioner from this case.

4. Conversely, learned Deputy Prosecutor General submits that prosecution has proved its case against the petitioner up to hilt while producing confidence inspiring evidence and finally prays for dismissal of this revision petition. Faiza Bibi and Naveed Ali (complainant and injured of the case, respectively, mentioned above) also oppose this petition.
5. Arguments heard and available record perused.

6. It has been noticed that as per case of prosecution mentioned in Fard Bayan (Ex.PA) got recorded by Faiza Bibi (complainant/PW-1) to Iftikhar Ahmad, A.S.I., on the basis of which F.I.R. (Ex.PB) was registered, is that Raju (present petitioner) while armed with pistol and Saqlain armed with pistol uttered abuses to Naveed Ali (husband of complainant lady); Raju raised lalkara and made straight firing at husband of complainant lady; one fire hit at thigh of right leg of Naveed and one fire hit at thigh of left leg whereas Saqlain fired shot with pistol which hit at left shin of Naveed, who after becoming injured, fell on the ground; Raju also gave Butt blows at face and head of Naveed, which resulted injuries to Naveed. However, Faiza Bibi (complainant of the case) while appearing before the Court as PW-1 during the trial stated that she saw that Ahsan alias Raju (present petitioner) made fire shot at her husband which hit on his left thigh and second fire on left shin (یپنڈل) and thereafter Saqlain Abbas snatched Criminal Revision No.8944 of 2026 5 pistol from Ahsan alias Raju and made fire on right thigh of her husband, Saqlain Abbas also gave beating through Butt of pistol on his head; in this regard, relevant portion of statement of complainant lady (PW-1) is reproduced as under: - “I also saw that Ahsan alias Raju made fire shot at my husband which hit on his left thigh (Putt) and second fire on his left shin (Pindli). After that Saqlain Abbas snatched Ahsan Ali alias Raju’s Pistol and made fire on right thigh (Putt) of my husband. After firing on his right thigh (Putt) Saqlain Abbas also beaten my husband through butt of pistol on his head while he was laying injured on ground, advance threats and run away on bike.”
(emphasis added)

It is, thus, evident that the complainant lady (PW-1) changed the stance/version initially set out in Fard Bayan (Ex.PA), on the basis of which, FIR (Ex.PB) was recorded, because in her initial version i.e. Fard Bayan (Ex.PA), she got recorded that Raju (present petitioner) made firing, one fire hit at thigh of right leg of Naveed and one fire hit at thigh of left leg whereas Saqlain fired shot with pistol which hit at left shin of Naveed and then Raju gave Butt blows at face and head of Naveed, which also resulted injuries to Naveed, but in her statement before the Court, she categorically stated that Ahsan alias Raju made fire shot at her husband which hit on his left thigh and second fire on left shin (یپنڈل) and thereafter Saqlain Abbas snatched pistol from Ahsan alias Raju and made firing on right thigh of her husband, Saqlain Abbas also gave beating through Butt of pistol on his head.

Similarly, Naveed Ali (injured of the case) while appearing before the Court as PW-2 during the trial stated that Ahsan alias Raju made straight firing on his left thigh and second fire on his left shin whereas accused Saqlain Abbas snatched pistol from Ahsan alias Raju and made fire shot on his right thigh and he (Saqlain Abbas) gave blow of pistol on his head; in this regard, relevant portion of his statement is reproduced as under: - “Ahsan alias Raju put his weapon and made straight fire on my left thigh (Putt) and second fire on my left shin (pindli). Accused Saqlian Abbas also snatched a Pistol from Ahsan alias Raju and made fire shot on my right thigh (Putt). I fallen down on the ground. Saqlian Abbas also made blow of pistol on my head and run away while abusing me.”
(emphasis added)

Criminal Revision No.8944 of 2026 6 Likewise, Muhammad Naeem (eyewitness) while appearing before the Court as PW-3 during the trial stated that he saw that Ahsan alias Raju made fire at husband of his sister namely Faiza on his left thigh and second fire on his left shin (یپنڈل) whereas Saqlain Abbas snatched pistol from Ahsan Ali alias Raju and made fire on right thigh of Naveed Ali and he (Saqlain Abbas) also gave beating with pistol at head of Naveed Ali; relevant portion of his statement in this regard reads as follows: - “We also saw that Ahsan alias Raju made fire at my sister Faiza's husband on his left thigh (Putt) and second fire on his left shin (Pindli). After that Saqlain Abbas snatched Ahsan Ali alias Raju's pistol and made fire on right thigh (Putt) of Naveed Ali. After firing on his right thigh (Putt) Saqlian Abbas also beaten the Naveed Ali's head with his pistol while he was laying injured on ground and advancing further threats and run away on bike.”
(emphasis added)

So, a comparison of the statements made by Faiza Bibi (complainant/PW-1), Naveed Ali (injured/PW-2) and Muhammad Naeem (eyewitness/PW-3) with the contents of Fard Bayan (Ex.PA) got recorded by complainant (PW-1) and FIR (Ex.PB), reflects major contradictions and variations. It has been also observed that Naveed Ali (injured of the case/PW-2) was medically examined vide MLC No.628/2023 (Ex.PG) and perusal whereof read together with statement of Dr. Haider Ali (PW-10), clearly reveals that no injury was found either on the face or on the head of Naveed Ali. It is also relevant to mention here that as per Fard Bayan (Ex.PA) of the complainant, F.I.R. (Ex.PB), statements of complainant (PW-1), Naveed Ali (injured/PW-2) and Muhammad Naeem (eyewitness/PW-3), Saqlain Abbas (co-accused) was also attributed effective role of causing firearm injury to Naveed Ali (injured of the case/PW-2) but when he has been acquitted in the case on the basis of same set of witnesses i.e. evidence vide aforementioned judgment dated: 22.04.2025 passed by learned Judicial Magistrate Section: 30, Lahore (trial court) which is still holding the field and any appeal has neither been filed by the State nor by the complainant party against said order of his acquittal as confirmed by learned Deputy Prosecutor General as well as Criminal Revision No.8944 of 2026 7 complainant lady (PW-1) and Naveed Ali (injured/PW-2), then said evidence now can only be relied and used against present petitioner if same is strongly corroborated by the independent evidence; in this regard, guidance has been sought from the cases of “Munir Ahmad and another versus The State and others” (2019 SCMR 79), “ALTAF HUSSAIN versus The STATE”

(2019 SCMR 274), “MUHAMMAD IDREES and another versus The STATE and others” (2021 SCMR 612), “PERVAIZ KHAN and another versus The STATE” (2022 SCMR 393), “RAFAQAT ALI versus The STATE” (2022 SCMR 1107), “SAJJAD HUSSAIN versus The STATE and others” (2022 SCMR 1540), “AMEERUDDIN versus The STATE” (PLD 2025 Supreme Court 383) and “UMER DRAZ and another versus THE STATE and others” (2026 SCMR 1185); relevant portion from the case of MUHAMMAD IDREES (Supra) is as follows: - “We further note that the ocular account of (PW-9) and (PW-10) has been disbelieved by the High Court, which we find was rightly disbelieved, against Muhammad Saleem who was alleged to have played a similar role in the occurrence, and he stands acquitted. Therefore, the same evidence cannot be relied upon to convict Muhammad Idrees, unless there is an independent corroboration of it to the extent of his involvement in commission of the offence. Recovery being inconsequential there is no corroborative evidence to distinguish the case of the petitioner from that of the acquitted accused.” Similarly, relevant portion from case of PERVAIZ KHAN (Supra) is hereby reproduced as under: - “The High Court through the impugned judgment concurred with the findings of the trial court regarding the acquittal of three co-accused who actively participated in the occurrence and their role was getting support from the medical evidence meaning thereby the witnesses of the ocular account have been disbelieved qua the said acquitted co-accused and their evidence cannot be taken into consideration against the present appellants in the absence of any corroboratory piece of evidence which is totally missing in this case because the FSL report to the extent of one of the appellant is negative and even no recovery was effected from the other appellant. Learned counsel for the complainant tried to distinguish the case of the present appellants from the case of the acquitted accused by saying that as present appellants firstly fired upon the deceased hence the subsequent firing by the remaining accused although has been disbelieved but cannot give any benefit to the appellants. This argument has no force because in the FIR and also during the trial all the witnesses of the ocular account remained consistent on the point that all the seven accused fired upon the Criminal Revision No.8944 of 2026 8 deceased persons and their bullets hit the deceased on different part of their bodies. So there is nothing on record to distinguish the role of the present appellants from the role of those accused who have been acquitted by the trial Court and their acquittal has been maintained by the High Court and further their acquittal was never challenged before this Court. Due to the above circumstances, the conviction and sentence of appellants is not sustainable on the same set of evidence, which was found doubtful to the extent of three acquitted co-accused.” It goes without saying that though empties and live bullets were secured from the place of occurrence and a pistol was allegedly recovered at the instance of present petitioner yet neither said pistol was exhibited in the Court nor any report of Punjab Forensic Science Agency was produced in evidence to establish that the empties secured from the place of occurrence matched with the pistol allegedly recovered from the petitioner. In the absence of such forensic corroboration, evidentiary value of the alleged recovery of pistol stands considerably diminished and, as such, said recovery, by itself, is of no avail to the case of prosecution.

As far as motive is concerned, as per own case of the prosecution, some days earlier to present occurrence, Raju etc. made altercation with Faisal who is brother of complainant lady and due to said grudge, instant occurrence took place; in this regard, relevant portion of statement of complainant (PW-1) is reproduced as under: - “Due to previous enmity with my brother Faisal and quarrelling between them due to this enmity, both above said accused persons took revenge of it by firing shots and injured my husband.”
(emphasis added)

Thus, motive was previous quarrel between Faisal (brother of complainant lady) and accused persons, and not with Naveed Ali (injured of the case/ PW-2); even Faisal (mentioned above) was not produced during trial of the case to prove said motive; therefore, motive has not been proved in the case. It is also relevant to mention here that while examining the petitioner as accused under Section: 342 Cr.P.C. during trial of the case, abscondence of the petitioner as well as report of Punjab Forensic Science Agency qua empties secured from the place of occurrence and allegedly recovered pistol at the Criminal Revision No.8944 of 2026 9 instance of the petitioner, were not put to him in order to have his explanation/reply in said regard, thus, these cannot be used against him for convicting and sentencing in the case; in this regard, case of “AMEER ZEB versus THE STATE” (PLD 2012 Supreme Court 380) can be safely referred and its relevant portion from Paragraph No.6 available at Page No.398, is hereby reproduced for ready reference:- “It is trite that a piece of evidence not put to the accused person at the time of recording of his statement under section 342, Cr.P.C. cannot be used against him by the prosecution.”
(emphasis added)

In this regard, guidance has also been sought from the case of “ABDUL HAYEE and ABDULLAH alias GHAZALI and another” (2025 SCMR 281) and relevant portion of the same from Paragraph No.14 is hereby reproduced as under:- “14. Insofar as the recoveries of weapons of offence from the petitioners in another case bearing FIR No. 121 dated 26.05.2009 under Sections 324/353/186/148/149 P.P.C., read with Section 13 of the Arms Ordinance, 1965 and Section 7 of the Anti Terrorism Act, 1997, at Police Station Mochh, District Mianwali, which recoveries were also relied upon by the prosecution in the instant case and positive reports of Forensic Science Laboratory are concerned, we have noted that the said recoveries were not put to the petitioners in their statements recorded under Section 342 Cr.P.C., therefore, the above-mentioned pieces of prosecution evidence cannot be considered against the petitioners and the same have rightly been discarded by the learned High Court in paragraph No. 15 of the impugned judgment. Reference in this context may also be made to the cases of, Fida Hussain Shah v. The State (2024 SCMR 1622), Haji Nawaz v. The State (2020 SCMR 687) and Mst. Anwar Begum v. Akhtar Hussain (2017 SCMR 1710).”

Similarly, case of “OBAIDULAH and 2 others versus The STATE and others” (2025 SCMR 1558) can be advantageously referred on the subject and relevant portion of the same from Paragraph No.7 available at Page Nos.1567- 1568 is hereby reproduced below:- “We have further noted that no motive was put to the petitioners in their statements recorded under Section 342, Cr.P.C. It is by now well settled that if a piece of evidence is not put to an accused in his statement recorded under Section 342, Cr.P.C, in order to provide him a chance to produce his defence against the said evidence then such evidence cannot be used against the accused. Reference in this context may be made to Criminal Revision No.8944 of 2026 10 the cases of Haji Nawaz v. The State (2020 SCMR 687) and Dr. Waqar Hameed v. The State (2020 SCMR 321). In the case of 'Haji Nawaz' (supra), this Court has held as under;- “The law is settled by now that if a piece of evidence or a circumstance is not put to an accused person at the time of recording his statement under section 342, Cr.P.C, then the same cannot be considered against him for the purpose of recording his conviction."

In the case of 'Dr. Waqar Hameed' (supra), this Court laid emphasis as follows:- "It is by now well settled that a piece of evidence which is not put to an accused while recording his statement under section 342, Code of Criminal Procedure cannot be used against him.””

Furthermore, judgment dated: 12.08.2026 passed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Criminal Petition No.753-L/2025 titled as “The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab versus Abid and another” can also be advantageously quoted on the subject and relevant portion of the same from Paragraph No.2 is hereby reproduced as under: - “It is pertinent to note that a piece of evidence not put to an accused at the time of recording his statement under section 342 Cr.P.C. cannot be used against him, and we hold that an unbroken chain of custody is pivotal to the prosecution's case in narcotics matters, the High Court found that, in the absence of the respondent having been confronted with this vital evidence, the prosecution case lost its foundation.” So far as medical evidence is concerned, it is trite law that medical evidence is mere supportive/confirmatory type of evidence and not the corroboratory piece of evidence, it can only tell about number, locale of injury, nature, magnitude of injury and kind of weapon used for causing injury but it cannot tell about identity of the assailant who caused the injury; therefore, same cannot provide any corroboration to the prosecution against the petitioner; in this regard guidance has been sought from the case of “NAVEED ASGHAR and two others versus The STATE” (PLD 2021 SC 600) and relevant portion from its Paragraph No.31 is hereby reproduced below: - “31. The prosecution has attempted to complete the chain of circumstantial evidence by medical evidence relating to the post mortem examinations of the deceased persons. This evidence proves only the factum that death of the deceased persons was caused by cutting their throats through some sharp edge weapon; it does in no way indicate who had cut their throats and with what particular weapon. Medical evidence is in the nature of supporting, confirmatory or explanatory of the direct or circumstantial evidence, and is not "corroborative evidence" in the Criminal Revision No.8944 of 2026 11 sense the term is used in legal parlance for a piece of evidence that itself also has some probative force to connect the accused person with the commission of offence. Medical evidence by itself does not throw any light on the identity of the offender. Such evidence may confirm the available substantive evidence with regard to certain facts including seat of the injury, nature of the injury, cause of the death, kind of the weapon used in the occurrence, duration between the injuries and the death, and presence of an injured witness or the injured accused at the place of occurrence, but it does not connect the accused with the commission of the offence. It cannot constitute corroboration for proving involvement of the accused person in the commission of offence, as it does not establish the identity of the accused person.

Therefore, the medical evidence is of little help to the prosecution for bringing home the guilt to the petitioners. In criminal law, corroboration needs to link the accused directly to the commission of crime rather than just proving a crime committed but no evidence, much less strong and independent evidence, to corroborate aforementioned ocular account against the petitioner is available on the record; hence, petitioner cannot be convicted on the basis of aforementioned set of witnesses i.e. evidence. However, this important and legal aspect appears to have escaped the attention of both the courts below while passing the impugned judgments against the present petitioner.

7. Nutshell of the above discussion is that impugned judgments against the petitioner are not sustainable. Therefore, for the safe administration of justice, instant criminal revision petition is allowed/accepted, both impugned judgments to the extent of petitioner are set-aside and consequently, convictions recorded against and sentences awarded to the petitioner vide judgment dated: 22.04.2025 passed by the trial court and upheld by the appellate court vide judgment dated: 17.01.2026, are also hereby set aside. The petitioner is acquitted of the charge, he be released from jail forthwith, if not required in any other case. (Farooq Haider)
Judge Approved for reporting (Farooq Haider)
